doc.title: Jack Lesberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

chapter: Boston youth and learning the bass
title: Violin family and after-hours clubs while at English High School
summary: Lesberg's violinist brother and sister, studying violin and viola with Carl Barladen, and playing Boston restaurants and after-hours clubs through high school.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: When you were a youth, was there music in your house a lot?

Quite a bit, yeah, actually. My brother was a professional violinist. He was about — let me see, Dave would have been — oh he was about 13 or 14 years older than I am. He was born in Russia actually. I was born in Boston in 1920. And my sister also played the violin. And I also took the violin. There is about six or seven years between us. There’s quite a spread in the family there. And I played the violin and viola, and studied with a very fine teacher at Boston, Carl Barladen was his name. He was with the Boston Symphony Orchestra under Karl Muok. It goes way back to those kind of names. But he was a very — and he was 80 years old at that time, Carl Barladen was. And so my brother and sister had both studied with him previously. And I played the violin and viola, and studied with him for about I guess five years or six years, and I played it around Boston in oh a couple of restaurants that had a little incidental music during the © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

dinner hour or something like that. And then I went on and I played in clubs. They had after hour clubs. And an after hour club was one that opened about eleven or twelve o’clock at night when the legitimate clubs so to speak were closing, and you could get a drink in there. And they had trios and quartets that consisted of either violin, the cello — not the cello — violin and guitar and bass, occasionally a piano might have been in there. And people used to come in there, and they were quite orderly places, and we worked, and they must have had about 18 or 20 of them all around the Boston area. They were very popular. And they would stay open until about five or six o’clock in the morning. And that’s what I used to do when I was going to my early years at English High School.
How did you stay awake in class?

Well it was just amazing. I was pretty good, fortunately I was pretty good with my studies too, so I used to do most of the homework there, on the study periods, and I managed to get out of the military training, they didn’t think I was too good at that so I had an extra study period there.
You had military training in the school?
Yeah, they had a training. It was a boys school, English High School, they had a girl’s version of it as well there, but they were city schools, very large schools.
